fixture_name: Six HAWK pedestrian crossings — US final design (FHWA case study, PD)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Night-time conspicuity of a HAWK display against competing background elements is a recognized, scheme-relevant safety issue that can delay driver stop decisions over pedestrians on an arterial.
justifications.evidence_grounding: The pivotal driver-confusion claim is supported by a verbatim quote from EV-US001 tied to the Speedway Blvd/Rook Ave site, satisfying the quote requirement for full credit.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly filed as a safety_concern with no normative_basis_note, keeping the safety observation categorically distinct from any compliance question under FHWA RSA semantics.
justifications.recommendation_quality: A reflective border around the HAWK signal is a specific, actionable, and viable conspicuity treatment directly matched to the competing-background-elements problem.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians are explicitly identified as the exposed road users if drivers misread or detect the beacon late, linking driver conspicuity to VRU protection as relevant here.

justifications.substance: Short pedestrian clearance intervals stranding slower/elderly walkers during conflicting releases at high-collision HAWK sites is a substantive, well-targeted final-design-stage signal-timing safety issue.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim is anchored by a verbatim quoted passage from EV-US-016 ('The pedestrian clearance interval may be short, particularly for elderly pedestrians') tied to the recorded FHWA case study issue for these exact sites.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a safety_concern under FHWA RSA semantics, distinct from any MUTCD compliance question, with no conflation of code adherence and safety risk.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Reprogramming clearance intervals at all six named HAWK crossings with a reduced assumed walking speed is specific, actionable, and feasible at final design stage.
justifications.vru_coverage: VRU impact is central and explicit: pedestrians and elderly pedestrians are named road users and the scenario confirms elderly pedestrians as the recorded focus of the issue.
